question: A community health nurse notices that several mothers in a rural village are refusing the polio vaccine due to rumors. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Engage community leaders and hold an educational meeting to address concerns
options.B: Administer the vaccines secretly without informing the parents
options.C: Report the entire village to law enforcement agencies for non-compliance
options.D: Stop visiting the village and focus only on compliant urban neighborhoods

explanation: Building trust through respectful dialogue and community engagement is the most effective nursing approach to overcome vaccine hesitancy. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h8)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading between patients in a ward?

options.A: Closing the windows to keep outdoor dust away
options.B: Consistent and proper hand hygiene by all staff
options.C: Burning all hospital bedsheets after a single use
options.D: Using scented air fresheners in the delivery room

explanation: You nailed it! Good hand hygiene is the number one defense against hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T15#GNS324_U5_T15_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of cardiac monitoring in a hospital setting?

options.A: Measuring exact blood pressure every few seconds
options.B: Calculating the total volume of blood pumped per minute
options.C: Checking the oxygen level inside red blood cells
options.D: Continuous tracking of heart rate and electrical rhythm

explanation: Cardiac monitors are specifically designed to watch the electrical activity and rate of the heart in real time. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h1)

question: Staff nurses complain of severe exhaustion. Instead of just adding extra shifts, the manager investigates and discovers that broken equipment is causing major delays. What has the manager found?

options.A: A completely unrelated administrative task
options.B: The root cause of the exhaustion
options.C: An entirely programmed routine choice
options.D: The personal fault of the junior nurses

explanation: Brilliant! By looking past the surface complaints, the manager found the true source of the trouble. [learn more](GST321_U1_T8#GST321_U1_T8_h4)

question: When is the best time to use a multiple line graph?

options.A: When displaying the exact percentages of a single pie chart
options.B: When comparing two or more related trends on the same set of axes
options.C: When listing text instructions for wound dressing changes
options.D: When only a single measurement is taken once in a lifetime

explanation: Correct! When you want to see how two or more groups stack up against each other over the same period, put them on one graph. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T10#GNS217_U4_T10_h3)

question: Which agency coordinates primary healthcare development at the national level in Nigeria?

options.A: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)

explanation: The NPHCDA is the main federal body guiding PHC implementation all across Nigeria. Good to know for Nigerian nursing practice! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a frequent cause of severe injuries on industrial cargo or work boats?

options.A: Falling debris from land-based skyscrapers
options.B: Sudden attacks by wild marine mammals on deck
options.C: Machinery entanglements and heavy winch failures
options.D: High-speed motor vehicle collisions at sea

explanation: Correct! Industrial ships have heavy gears and winches that can unfortunately cause serious mechanical injuries to the crew. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h4)

question: Why is an obstetric ultrasound often performed when evaluating a patient with severe hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: To check for multiple gestation or molar pregnancy
options.B: To see if the liver is enlarged from fluid backup
options.C: To measure the exact thickness of the stomach lining
options.D: To test the baby's hearing and nervous system

explanation: Conditions like twins or a molar pregnancy cause much higher levels of hormones, which can trigger worse vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for cleansing a medication vial rubber top with an alcohol swab?

options.A: To reduce the risk of introducing microorganisms into the vial
options.B: To remove sticky price tags left by the hospital pharmacy
options.C: To warm up the medication liquid inside the glass container
options.D: To make the rubber top softer for the needle to pierce

explanation: Wiping the access port with alcohol reduces surface bacteria and prevents introducing pathogens into sterile solutions. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why do nurses need to handle strong chemical sterilants like glutaraldehyde with extra care?

options.A: They instantly blow up under bright theatre lamps
options.B: They can cause bad skin rashes, irritation, and breathing trouble
options.C: They completely cancel out the local anaesthetic given to patients
options.D: They melt stainless steel instruments into liquid on contact

explanation: Potent disinfectants are harsh on living cells! We always need good ventilation and protective gear to keep these chemicals away from our skin and lungs. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T12#GNS123_U5_T12_h4)

question: What does the 'Proximity Principle' mean when dealing with hazardous waste?

options.A: It should be shipped overseas to countries with large open spaces
options.B: It must be stored as far away from human populations as possible
options.C: It must be kept in temporary storage for at least ten years
options.D: It should be disposed of as close to its source as possible

explanation: You got it! Keeping travel distances short means fewer chances for accidental spills or exposure while moving dangerous materials around. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h3)

question: What is the correct way to fix a writing mistake on a paper patient chart?

options.A: Scratch the incorrect word out completely until it is totally unreadable.
options.B: Apply liquid correction fluid over the mistake and write neatly on top.
options.C: Rip the entire page out of the treatment book and start a fresh one.
options.D: Draw a single line through the error, write mistaken entry, and sign it.

explanation: You got it! A single neat line shows transparency. Never use Tipp-Ex or scribble words out completely—hiding mistakes looks like tampering. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which blood vessel is most often blocked in major strokes affecting the pons?

options.A: Anterior communicating artery
options.B: Middle cerebral artery
options.C: Internal carotid artery
options.D: Basilar artery

explanation: The basilar artery runs right along the front surface of the pons, supplying the blood it desperately needs to function. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h5)

question: What waste product does the liver make when processing extra amino acids?

options.A: Lactic acid
options.B: Bile salt
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Urea

explanation: The liver takes toxic ammonia from protein breakdown and turns it into safer urea so your kidneys can easily flush it out. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h6)

question: Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red blood cells?

options.A: Type O
options.B: Type B
options.C: Type AB
options.D: Type A

explanation: Type O is a true lifesaver! Its red blood cells don't have A or B antigens on them, so recipient antibodies won't panic and attack them. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T12#GNS311_U2_T12_h2)

question: A new mother on her third day postpartum says her breasts are hard, warm, and very painful. What is likely going on?

options.A: A blocked lactiferous duct due to tight clothing
options.B: Physiological engorgement as milk production begins in large volumes
options.C: Acute mastitis caused by a bacterial infection from the infant's mouth
options.D: Absence of oxytocin release during feedings

explanation: This is standard postpartum breast engorgement! The sudden rush of milk, blood, and fluids can make the breasts feel very full and tender around day three. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T17#GNS121_U5_T17_h5)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for stimulating the gallbladder to release bile?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Gastrin
options.C: Secretin
options.D: Cholecystokinin

explanation: Cholecystokinin is released when fats and proteins enter the small intestine, prompting the gallbladder to contract and release stored bile. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why do nurses use slide sheets when moving a patient from a bed to a stretcher?

options.A: They replace the need for any nurses to assist
options.B: They act as a heating pad to warm up the patient
options.C: They automatically record the patient's weight
options.D: They reduce friction and shearing forces on the patient's skin

explanation: Slide sheets are a nurse's best friend! They make patients glide smoothly, protecting fragile skin from friction and saving your back from strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h8)

question: Which ethical principle guides triage nurses to treat every patient fairly, no matter their background?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Paternalism
options.C: Justice
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Justice means treating everyone fairly and sharing our healthcare resources impartially, without any bias or favoritism. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting regular quality assurance audits in a day care facility?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any daily nursing supervision
options.B: To identify areas for improvement and maintain high standards of client safety
options.C: To increase daily attendance fees for participating families
options.D: To find staff members to blame when minor mistakes occur

explanation: Quality assurance reviews examine incident logs and procedures systematically to improve safety, prevent errors, and ensure regulatory compliance. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h8)

question: A patient asks if they can crush a sustained-release tablet because they have trouble swallowing large pills. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Contact the prescriber or pharmacist to find an alternative liquid form
options.B: Dissolve the whole pill in a glass of warm water
options.C: Crush the pill thoroughly and mix it with applesauce
options.D: Cut the pill in half using a tablet cutter

explanation: Crushing sustained-release or enteric-coated medications destroys their special delivery mechanism, leading to a dangerous surge of the drug all at once. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of these checks is a key part of a neurovascular assessment on an injured arm or leg?

options.A: Total daily fluid intake and urine output
options.B: Bowel sound frequency and abdominal tone
options.C: Peripheral pulses and capillary refill
options.D: Client baseline blood cholesterol levels

explanation: Well done! Neurovascular checks are all about blood flow, feeling, and movement. Checking pulses and capillary refill tells us if blood is reaching the fingers and toes. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why might a patient's surgical incision fail to heal properly due to poor diet?

options.A: The body lacks the necessary chemical building blocks for tissue repair
options.B: Patients who eat poorly refuse to take their prescribed painkillers
options.C: Dietary deficiencies completely stop blood circulation
options.D: Poor nutrition automatically causes surgical site infections

explanation: Cellular growth and tissue mending require specific nutrients like proteins and vitamins; without them, the body cannot effectively close wounds. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h1)

question: Why do myoblasts stop dividing before they fuse into myotubes?

options.A: To allow nerve endings to attach before the muscle membrane forms
options.B: Because the surrounding bone tissue physically blocks further cell division
options.C: To begin synthesizing contractile proteins and organizing into fibers
options.D: Because they run out of oxygen supply in the early embryo

explanation: Once they stop multiplying, the cells focus all their energy on building the proteins (like actin and myosin) needed for muscle contraction. Keep up the brilliant work! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h2)

question: Between which tracheal rings do surgeons usually perform a tracheotomy?

options.A: Between the tenth and eleventh rings
options.B: Between the cricoid and the first ring
options.C: Between the second and third rings
options.D: Between the sixth and seventh rings

explanation: Surgeons love the space between the 2nd and 3rd tracheal rings because it helps them steer clear of major blood vessels and upper neck structures. Great detail to remember for clinicals! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the folded outer layer of the brain called?

options.A: Cerebral cortex
options.B: Brainstem
options.C: Spinal cord
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: The cerebral cortex is the outer layer of neural tissue folded into gyri and sulci to maximize brain cell surface area. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h1)

question: During a physical assessment of a patient with second-week enteric fever, which organs are you most likely to find enlarged?

options.A: Liver and spleen
options.B: Adrenal glands
options.C: Thyroid and parathyroid
options.D: Kidneys and pancreas

explanation: You nailed it! The bacteria loves to hide and multiply in the body's filtering tissues, leading to a swollen liver and spleen (hepatosplenomegaly). [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h3)

question: Which test is commonly used to check a patient's long-term blood sugar control over the past three months?

options.A: Hemoglobin A1c assay
options.B: Serum potassium level
options.C: Urinalysis for protein
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: Correct! The HbA1c test gives us a wonderful 3-month picture of how well blood glucose has been managed. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h3)

question: What does nutrient utilisation mean in the human body?

options.A: Storing excess fat directly beneath the skin layers
options.B: The rapid excretion of waste products through the kidneys
options.C: The physical chewing and swallowing of solid meals
options.D: Converting ingested food into energy and structural components

explanation: You've got this! Nutrient utilisation is simply how the body takes down food molecules and turns them into useful energy and building blocks for the body. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h1)

question: When cancer treatment cannot cure the disease, but aims to stop tumor growth and extend life, what is this main goal called?

options.A: Palliation
options.B: Cure
options.C: Prevention
options.D: Control

explanation: You've got this! When complete cure isn't possible, 'control' is the goal—stopping the cancer from spreading further to help the patient live a longer, fuller life. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which communication approach is best for building personal trust and clearing up doubts?

options.A: Newspaper advertisements
options.B: National television broadcasts
options.C: Billboards along major highways
options.D: Interpersonal communication

explanation: Nothing beats face-to-face talk! It lets you have a two-way chat where patients can ask questions and share their deepest concerns. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h4)

question: Which patient is the best candidate for a routine fasting blood sugar screening?

options.A: A young child recovering from a normal cold
options.B: A healthy athlete with mild muscle soreness after running
options.C: An adult with obesity and a family history of diabetes
options.D: An elderly patient admitted with a broken bone from a fall

explanation: Great thinking! People with risk factors like extra weight and a family history are prime candidates for routine checks so we catch issues early. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h2)

question: Which type of nutrient is especially important for the baby's brain and nervous system growth?

options.A: Water
options.B: Fats
options.C: Starch
options.D: Fiber

explanation: Healthy dietary fats are superstars here! They provide essential fatty acids that build brain tissue and support your baby's developing nervous system. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h3)

question: What is the main job of specific objectives in a research study?

options.A: To list the names of all nurses participating in the study
options.B: To provide background history on the hospital ward
options.C: To break down the general objective into smaller, measurable tasks
options.D: To replace the need for a detailed literature review

explanation: Think of specific objectives as the baby steps that break your big main goal into manageable, actionable pieces. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the medical term for a resting heart rate that stays above 100 beats per minute?

options.A: Bradycardia
options.B: Asystole
options.C: Arrhythmia
options.D: Tachycardia

explanation: Tachy- means fast! So when a resting heart rate races above 100 beats per minute, we call it tachycardia. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which vitamin is especially important in early pregnancy to help prevent neural tube defects in the baby?

options.A: Vitamin E
options.B: Vitamin K
options.C: Folate
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: You nailed it! Folate (or folic acid) is vital during the early weeks of pregnancy to help the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h7)

question: What happens right away to the tissue when teeth pierce the skin?

options.A: The body instantly creates a permanent protective scar barrier
options.B: The immune system seals the puncture wound with sterile fluid
options.C: All surrounding blood vessels dilate to neutralize the foreign saliva
options.D: Oral bacteria are pushed directly into sterile tissue planes

explanation: The sheer mechanical action of a bite breaks the skin barrier and inoculates mouth germs straight into the vulnerable underlying tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h2)

question: Which area in the brainstem acts as the main control center coordinating the urination reflex?

options.A: Pontine micturition center
options.B: Hypothalamic nucleus
options.C: Medulla oblongata
options.D: Substantia nigra

explanation: Spot on! The pontine micturition center in the brainstem orchestrates the whole process—telling the bladder to squeeze while telling the sphincters to relax. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h5)

question: In nursing and science, what does 'pH' stand for?

options.A: Power of hydration
options.B: Pressure of homeostasis
options.C: Potential of hydrogen
options.D: Percentage of hydroxyl

explanation: pH simply stands for the 'potential of hydrogen'. It tells us how many free hydrogen ions are floating around in a fluid, which determines how acidic or basic it is! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h1)

question: What activity rule should you teach a patient before they go home after a liver biopsy?

options.A: Eat no solid foods for the next five days
options.B: Avoid heavy lifting and hard exercise for at least a week
options.C: Stay in bed in a dark room for two whole weeks
options.D: Keep your right arm strapped in a sling for two days

explanation: Spot on! Straining or lifting increases pressure inside the belly, which can trigger bleeding even days later. Rest is key! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h7)

question: What does setting up a 'digital curfew' mean for healthy screen habits?

options.A: Turning off and putting away screens at least one hour before bedtime
options.B: Banning the purchase of new smartphones for teenagers under eighteen
options.C: Charging mobile phones directly underneath the pillow while sleeping
options.D: Shutting down the entire neighborhood Wi-Fi router at midnight

explanation: A digital curfew is a great self-care habit: putting the phone away an hour before sleep lets your mind relax and prepare for deep rest. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why is proper cleaning and drying of nebulizer equipment so critical for patient safety?

options.A: Dirty equipment will permanently break the air compressor motor
options.B: Washing prevents the plastic mask from changing color over time
options.C: Moist plastic parts easily grow harmful bacteria that can cause lung infections
options.D: Leftover medication residue turns into a solid metal inside the tube

explanation: Wet nebulizer cups are breeding grounds for germs, which the patient would inhale directly into their lungs during the next treatment. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)

question: Why is the global population of older adults increasing?

options.A: Decreased migration of younger populations
options.B: Higher infant mortality rates in rural areas
options.C: Lower birth rates and longer life expectancies
options.D: Stricter laws regarding retirement age

explanation: As people live longer and fewer children are born, the overall proportion of older adults in the population rises. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h2)

question: What should a nursing unit manager do immediately after setting targets with the staff?

options.A: Punish nurses who ask questions about the goals
options.B: File the document away until the end of the year
options.C: Hand over all leadership duties to junior staff
options.D: Support staff in carrying out daily duties toward those targets

explanation: After goals are set, the actual work phase begins where staff execute plans and management provides support. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main drawback of traditional incremental budgeting?

options.A: It requires every single nurse to have a degree in accounting
options.B: It completely stops all purchases of new hospital equipment
options.C: It can carry forward wasteful spending from past years without question
options.D: It takes too much time to calculate compared to zero-based budgeting

explanation: Because incremental budgeting just adds to old totals, past inefficiencies often get repeated automatically. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to give sugary drinks to an unconscious patient with low blood sugar?

options.A: The stomach will reject all sugary liquids
options.B: It can cause choking or enter the lungs
options.C: It will immediately cause a diabetic coma
options.D: It takes three days for the body to digest it

explanation: An unconscious patient cannot protect their airway. Giving them fluids by mouth can cause aspiration, sending liquid straight into their lungs. Safety first! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T19#GNS222_U2_T19_h7)

question: How do growing follicles signal the brain just before ovulation happens?

options.A: By releasing high levels of estrogen that create a positive feedback loop
options.B: By producing large amounts of progesterone to slow down hormone release
options.C: By stopping all hormonal signals to let the brain rest
options.D: By secreting inhibin to completely block luteinizing hormone production

explanation: As follicles grow, they pump out high levels of estrogen. This switches the body into a positive feedback loop, which sparks the big LH release! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the main difference between phantom limb sensation and phantom limb pain?

options.A: Pain only happens during the day, while sensation occurs exclusively while sleeping.
options.B: Sensation means the limb is still there, while pain means the nerve has died completely.
options.C: Pain is purely psychological, while sensation is caused by poor blood flow.
options.D: Sensation involves normal feelings like tingling, while pain involves burning or shooting hurt.

explanation: Phantom sensation is just a harmless awareness that the limb is missing (like feeling an itchy toe), whereas phantom pain is actual uncomfortable, shooting distress. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h5)

question: What is the main focus of modern recovery-oriented psychiatric nursing?

options.A: Confining patients indefinitely in secure institutional facilities
options.B: Helping individuals live meaningful lives despite mental health challenges
options.C: Relying exclusively on physical restraints during behavioral crises
options.D: Ignoring social factors in favor of strict medication compliance

explanation: Today's psychiatric nursing is all about recovery. We empower patients to chase their personal goals, live independently, and find real wellness. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h8)

question: No matter how advanced hospital technology gets, what will always remain the nurse's primary challenge?

options.A: Balancing machine intelligence with compassionate human care
options.B: Finding enough electrical outlets to charge wearable patches
options.C: Convincing hospital administrators to buy cheaper equipment
options.D: Learning how to repair broken computer microchips

explanation: Spot on! Machines can crunch numbers and track drips, but nursing fundamentally depends on your human empathy, touch, and critical thinking. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h7)

question: How do barrier methods like condoms actually prevent STIs?

options.A: To permanently neutralize circulating viral loads in the bloodstream
options.B: To increase local mucosal immunity against parasitic invasion
options.C: To block the exchange of infectious bodily fluids during intercourse
options.D: To destroy bacterial cell walls upon contact in the vaginal canal

explanation: You got it! Condoms act as a physical shield so infectious fluids don't pass between partners. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the medical term for seeing double, which happens when the nerves controlling eye movement are messed up?

options.A: Mydriasis
options.B: Ptosis
options.C: Diplopia
options.D: Strabismus

explanation: Diplopia is just the clinical word for double vision. It occurs when the tiny muscles around the eyes aren't working together smoothly. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h5)

question: Why should a food pantry be located away from the kitchen stove or oven?

options.A: To keep the kitchen floor clear of heavy storage bins
options.B: To protect the food from damaging heat and fluctuating temperatures
options.C: To ensure the pantry door opens without hitting the stove
options.D: To prevent the oven smoke from flavoring the dry goods

explanation: Constant heat from cooking appliances can spoil dry goods and make oils go rancid much faster. Keep them cool! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h3)

question: In public health, what term is commonly used instead of 'accident' for injuries that happen without bad intentions?

options.A: Intentional injuries
options.B: Unintentional injuries
options.C: Spontaneous trauma
options.D: Stochastic events

explanation: Great job! Public health experts prefer 'unintentional injuries' because most events we call accidents can actually be predicted and prevented. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which part of a reflex arc carries the action command away from the spinal cord to the muscle?

options.A: Afferent neuron
options.B: Efferent neuron
options.C: Cranial nerve bridge
options.D: Sensory receptor

explanation: That's correct! Efferent neurons ('E' for exit) carry the final command out from the spinal cord to tell the muscle or gland what to do. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h8)

question: What does a low Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) mostly point to during a community screening?

options.A: Normal muscle development
options.B: Risk of acute malnutrition
options.C: Excess visceral fat storage
options.D: Elevated serum cholesterol

explanation: Well done! MUAC is a quick, life-saving tool we use in community health to spot wasting and acute malnutrition in children and mothers. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h5)

question: What should a QA committee do if there is a sudden increase in surgical wound infections?

options.A: Close the entire hospital permanently
options.B: Blame the patients for having weak immune systems
options.C: Ignore the data because infections are normal after surgery
options.D: Investigate sterilization practices and surgical routines right away

explanation: You got it! A sudden jump in infections is a red flag that requires an immediate check of theatre and ward cleanliness. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which body system controls the release of hormones that trigger puberty?

options.A: Hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
options.B: Sympathetic-adrenomedullary pathway
options.C: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis
options.D: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system

explanation: Well done! The HPG axis is the body's master control center for releasing the sex hormones that drive all those physical changes during puberty. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h2)

question: A nurse manager uses a directive approach with a nursing student on day one, but gives more independence by week eight. Which leadership concept does this show?

options.A: Transactional compliance
options.B: Laissez-faire neglect
options.C: Situational leadership
options.D: Autocratic rigidity

explanation: Changing your leadership style as the learner gains confidence and skill is the definition of situational leadership. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is usually the very first step when putting together a new healthcare budget?

options.A: Borrowing large sums of money from local commercial banks
options.B: Reviewing past financial data and current patient trends
options.C: Firing staff to immediately reduce operational expenses
options.D: Purchasing expensive new diagnostic medical equipment

explanation: Before you can plan for tomorrow, you need to check yesterday. Looking at past records and patient numbers gives you a realistic starting point. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to ensure community members participate in a nutrition program?

options.A: Mobilizing community volunteers for distribution
options.B: Imposing strict rules without asking local opinions
options.C: Involving local leaders in the planning stages
options.D: Designing culturally appropriate interventions

question: What is the role of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

question: Why do we use Boolean words like AND and OR when searching research databases?

question: What is a major consequence when young girls experience unplanned early pregnancies?

question: Why should nurses understand the role of informal health providers in Nigeria?

question: Why is data analysis a critical step before planning any healthcare intervention?

question: Why do patients on blood thinners still rely on their body's natural healing to clear old clots?

question: Which of these is a major risk factor for getting perineal tears when having your first baby?

question: What should you tell a patient who says they need their rescue SABA inhaler multiple times every day?

question: Which part of the inner ear turns sound vibrations into electrical signals for the brain?

question: Why are fiber and low-fat diets important for long-term HIV care?

options.D: By using physical or chemical barriers to stop contamination
