question: A patient at a local clinic says they want to stop their modern epilepsy drugs and use unverified traditional herbs instead. As a nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Explain the risks of stopping medication abruptly and discuss how to safely manage the condition together
options.B: Threaten to report the patient to local authorities if they miss a single clinic appointment
options.C: Advise the patient to stop the medication immediately to see what happens
options.D: Tell the patient that traditional remedies are completely harmless and can replace drugs

explanation: Always meet patients with empathy and respect. Instead of judging, gently educate them on why stopping their meds is dangerous while working together to support their overall health journey. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h8)

question: What happens when a nurse washes their hands properly between patients?

options.A: It permanently cures the patient of chronic illnesses
options.B: It creates a new portal of entry for beneficial flora
options.C: It breaks the mode of transmission link in the chain
options.D: It destroys the genetic material of the reservoir host

explanation: Handwashing removes or kills germs, stopping them from traveling from one person to another. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h2)

question: What is a very common reason a doctor orders a proctoscopy for a patient with bright red blood in their stool?

options.A: Hemorrhoids
options.B: Gallstones
options.C: Gastric ulcers
options.D: Appendicitis

explanation: Spot on! Hemorrhoids are one of the most frequent causes of bright red rectal bleeding that doctors investigate with a proctoscopy. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the medical term for an infection and inflammation of the meninges?

options.A: Meningitis
options.B: Hematoma
options.C: Neuritis
options.D: Encephalitis

explanation: Easy peasy! Whenever you see '-itis' at the end of a medical word, it means inflammation. So, inflammation of the meninges is meningitis. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T8#GNS211_U3_T8_h7)

question: Which hormone do the kidneys produce to tell the bone marrow to make red blood cells?

options.A: Thrombopoietin
options.B: Erythropoietin
options.C: Calcitonin
options.D: Melatonin

explanation: Brilliant! When oxygen levels drop, the kidneys send out erythropoietin (EPO) as a rescue signal to the bone marrow to make more red blood cells. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T7#GNS121_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why do hospitals carry out job performance evaluations for nurses?

options.A: To punish nurses who make minor documentation mistakes
options.B: To measure care quality and guide professional growth
options.C: To find reasons to reduce staff salaries each year
options.D: To replace daily supervision and peer feedback entirely

explanation: Evaluations aren't meant to witch-hunt! They help check how we are doing against professional standards so we can keep our patients safe and grow in our nursing careers. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h1)

question: Why are bedside nurses often called the primary line of defense against patient harm?

options.A: They have the legal authority to rewrite physician prescriptions
options.B: They conduct all hospital administrative audits independently
options.C: They spend the most direct time observing subtle status changes
options.D: They make the final diagnostic decisions for every admission

explanation: You got it! Because nurses are always around patients, they easily notice early changes in a patient's condition and can step in before small issues become emergencies. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h1)

question: What happens to the color absorption properties of hemoglobin when it binds with oxygen?

options.A: It absorbs more red light and less infrared light
options.B: It absorbs more infrared light and less red light
options.C: It turns the surrounding plasma completely dark blue
options.D: It stops absorbing all types of light completely

explanation: Oxygenated hemoglobin absorbs infrared light differently than deoxygenated hemoglobin, which allows the oximeter sensor to measure the ratio. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h2)

question: What does a long streak of data points falling entirely on one side of the median line on a run chart mean?

options.A: That the data collection plan was written incorrectly
options.B: That patients are refusing to answer nurse surveys
options.C: A random coincidence caused by broken computer printers
options.D: A meaningful shift or special cause variation in the process

explanation: You've got this! A long unbroken streak on one side tells us something real has changed in the system—it's not just random luck. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which Nigerian federal agency enforces environmental standards, including healthcare waste rules?

options.A: FRSC
options.B: NESREA
options.C: NYSC
options.D: NAPTIP

explanation: That's right! NESREA is the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency in Nigeria. You're doing brilliantly! [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h8)

question: What is a common dietary trap patients fall into when starting a low-fat diet?

options.A: Eating too many leafy green vegetables every day
options.B: Consuming too much lean skinless chicken breast
options.C: Replacing healthy fats with large amounts of sugary foods
options.D: Drinking excessive amounts of plain filtered water

explanation: When foods lose their fat content, they can taste bland. Patients often make the mistake of loading up on sweets and refined carbs to compensate, which messes with blood sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h5)

question: What is polypharmacy generally defined as?

options.A: Stopping all medications abruptly without advice
options.B: Taking five or more medications concurrently
options.C: Injecting a single drug twice a day
options.D: Using only traditional herbs for chronic illnesses

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to the use of multiple drugs at the same time, commonly set at a threshold of five or more. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when planning an IEC activity?

options.A: Printing out colorful posters and flyers
options.B: Choosing which radio station will broadcast
options.C: Evaluating the final budget and expenses
options.D: Situation analysis and community assessment

explanation: Before jumping into action, a great nurse always checks the ground realities. You need to understand the community's actual needs and culture first! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h2)

question: Where do the best nursing research ideas usually spark from?

options.A: Everyday clinical observations
options.B: Hospital financial statements
options.C: Government tax reports
options.D: Pharmaceutical marketing brochures

explanation: Think about things you notice right on the ward! The challenges and patterns you see during clinical rotations make the most meaningful research topics. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h2)

question: A patient gets confused by heavy medical jargon you used. Where did the communication break down?

options.A: During the decoding phase
options.B: During the feedback generation
options.C: During the sender's encoding
options.D: During the channel selection

explanation: Exactly! Decoding is when the listener tries to make sense of your words—complex medical terms make this step tough. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why should you always share your assessment findings back with the community members who helped you?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to write clinical notes
options.B: It builds trust and encourages active community commitment
options.C: It stops patients from ever visiting the clinic again
options.D: It is required to collect fines from households

explanation: Sharing your findings shows respect for their time and input, and it makes them proud partners in solving their own health challenges! [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h6)

question: Why must community health nurses pay close attention to the well-being of family caregivers?

options.A: Caregivers are prone to severe physical and emotional burnout due to heavy demands
options.B: Caregiver stress prevents older adults from ever taking prescription drugs
options.C: Caregivers are legally responsible for paying all hospital nursing salaries
options.D: Caregivers usually suffer from the exact same infectious diseases as patients

explanation: Looking after an older relative without enough support can overwhelm a caregiver, making it crucial for nurses to monitor and assist them. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving ovulation-stimulating medications like clomiphene citrate?

options.A: To thicken the uterine lining permanently
options.B: To clear blocked fallopian tubes
options.C: To increase male testosterone levels
options.D: To encourage the release of mature eggs

explanation: These helpful drugs nudge the ovaries to develop and release eggs when a woman's ovulation is irregular. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h4)

question: How is the outside of the home visiting bag treated during a visit?

options.A: As a clean working surface
options.B: As sterile and clean
options.C: As contaminated
options.D: As safe for food storage

explanation: The outside of the bag touches various surfaces during travel and home entry, so it is always treated as contaminated. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why is figuring out how a chemical entered the body so important for your nursing care?

options.A: It replaces the need for vital sign monitoring during triage
options.B: It confirms the exact chemical formula without laboratory testing
options.C: It determines the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: It guides immediate decontamination steps and predicts systemic risks

explanation: Knowing the entry route helps you act fast—like washing skin or flushing eyes—and lets you anticipate which body organs are in the greatest danger. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T5#GNS215_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which two organs do the heaviest lifting when it comes to breaking down and removing hormones?

options.A: Pancreas and spleen
options.B: Lungs and skin
options.C: Liver and kidneys
options.D: Stomach and intestines

explanation: Your liver chemically alters and breaks down used hormones, while your kidneys filter the leftovers out into your urine. Great tag-team work! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h7)

question: What naturally happens to the outer layer of the skin as a person ages?

options.A: It becomes thinner and loses its elasticity
options.B: It produces significantly more sweat and oil
options.C: It permanently changes its original pigmentation
options.D: It grows thicker and develops more fat layers

explanation: As we age, our skin loses collagen and the epidermis gets thinner. This makes older adults' skin much more fragile and prone to tears or bruises. Good to keep in mind during daily care! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h2)

question: What does it mean when the cervical dilation curve crosses the action line on a partograph?

options.A: The baby is ready to be delivered immediately
options.B: Labor is progressing faster than normal limits
options.C: Intervention or timely referral is urgently required
options.D: The mother has entered the fourth stage of labor

explanation: Crossing the action line signals prolonged labor, prompting healthcare workers to take corrective action or transfer the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: Why might a woman with Type III FGM need a procedure called defibulation during childbirth?

options.A: To prevent severe postpartum hemorrhage from the uterus
options.B: To allow the baby to pass through the narrowed vaginal opening
options.C: To correct an underlying urinary tract infection
options.D: To speed up the delivery of the placenta

explanation: Spot on! The scar tissue seal blocks the birth canal, so healthcare providers must surgically open the area during labor to keep mother and baby safe. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why do mothers who have given birth before (multiparous women) often feel stronger afterpains than first-time mothers?

options.A: Their perineal wounds are always surgically larger
options.B: They are more sensitive to standard doses of analgesics
options.C: They produce significantly less lochia than primiparous mothers
options.D: Their uterine muscles lose tone and contract intermittently with greater force

explanation: Because her uterus has worked before, it doesn't stay clamped down all at once. Instead, it relaxes and contracts rhythmically, leading to stronger cramps as it gets back into shape. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h4)

question: Which of these is a key sign of Conduct Disorder rather than Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD)?

options.A: Argues frequently with adult authority figures
options.B: Destruction of property and hurting animals
options.C: Blames others for their own mistakes
options.D: Loses temper easily when asked to clean

explanation: Conduct disorder involves severe violations of rules and laws, such as property destruction and physical aggression, which go beyond simple defiance. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T1#GNS314_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) in Nigeria?

options.A: To pay retirement benefits for retired federal medical doctors
options.B: To import expensive surgical equipment for private clinics
options.C: To finance basic minimum health services at the primary care level
options.D: To build specialized teaching hospitals in every state capital

explanation: Well done! The BHCPF is set up specifically to pump money into primary healthcare, ensuring everyday community needs like immunizations are covered. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for establishing trust during a genitourinary assessment?

options.A: To eliminate the requirement for formal medical documentation
options.B: To prevent the need for diagnostic laboratory tests
options.C: To speed up the physical examination process
options.D: To encourage the patient to share sensitive health details

explanation: Genitourinary symptoms involve private bodily functions, making trust essential for an honest and accurate patient history. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h1)

question: A patient says they feel constantly terrified for no clear reason and cannot go to work. How should you as a nurse view this?

options.A: As a normal reaction to everyday life pressures that will resolve on its own
options.B: As a physical sign of a primary cardiac event rather than psychological distress
options.C: As an attention-seeking behavior requiring behavioral redirection
options.D: As an abnormal, pathological anxiety response that requires clinical evaluation

explanation: Great clinical thinking! When fear is constant, unprovoked, and stops someone from living their life, it goes way beyond normal worry and needs professional care. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h1)

question: An experienced nurse is bored with routine duties and wants to take on hospital quality projects. What management approach fits best?

options.A: Reducing the nurse's daily patient assignment size
options.B: Focusing strictly on increasing the base hourly salary
options.C: Threatening disciplinary action for minor paperwork delays
options.D: Providing opportunities for professional achievement and growth

explanation: You nailed it! When a nurse is looking for a challenge, giving them room to grow and achieve is the best way to keep them inspired. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which of these is an example of a strong system-level fix to prevent errors?

options.A: Redesigning automated medication dispensing cabinets to require double scans
options.B: Warning staff that future mistakes will result in immediate termination
options.C: Removing all safety policies to let nurses rely entirely on instinct
options.D: Telling nurses to pay closer attention so they never get tired

explanation: Brilliant! Changing technology and workflows creates a strong safety net that protects against human error much better than just telling staff to be careful. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h7)

question: A nurse is planning care for a patient just discharged from a long-stay asylum. What is the best initial approach based on community mental health principles?

options.A: Advise the family to keep the patient strictly locked inside the house
options.B: Encourage the patient to move to a distant city away from everyone
options.C: Stop all monitoring since the patient is now outside the hospital
options.D: Connect the patient with local clinic follow-ups and family support programs

explanation: Brilliant! Community care is all about continuous local support, outpatient check-ups, and keeping the patient engaged with their loved ones. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a smart way to make healthcare more cost-effective?

options.A: Investing heavily in community preventive care
options.B: Purchasing only expensive brand-name medications
options.C: Promoting the use of safe generic drugs
options.D: Shifting routine tasks to trained support cadres

explanation: Well done! Buying only pricey brand-name drugs wastes money when safe, affordable generic options work just as well. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h7)

question: Which chemical messenger do anticholinergic drugs block in the bladder?

options.A: Dopamine
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Think of acetylcholine as the trigger messenger. Anticholinergics block it from binding to receptors, preventing unwanted muscle squeezes. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T5#GNS223_U8_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of health care financing in a national health system?

options.A: Raising, pooling, and allocating funds for health services
options.B: Purchasing pharmaceutical manufacturing plants
options.C: Recruiting international medical volunteers
options.D: Setting international medical licensing examinations

explanation: Health financing is specifically concerned with how money is collected, combined, and spent to provide health care to the population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h1)

question: How should a nurse respond when a patient talks about a frightening delusion?

options.A: Tell the client that police are on their way to arrest them
options.B: Argue aggressively until the client admits the belief is false
options.C: Acknowledge the emotional distress without validating the false belief
options.D: Ignore the statement completely and change the subject

explanation: Well done! Show empathy for how scary the feeling is, but don't agree with the unreal belief. It keeps trust strong! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T3#GNS324_U4_T3_h6)

question: What makes a piece of writing a primary literature source?

options.A: It is a textbook summary written years after the original event occurred
options.B: It is an encyclopedia entry explaining general nursing theories
options.C: It is a library catalog used to locate published journal articles
options.D: It is a first-hand account written by the researchers who conducted the study

explanation: Brilliant! Primary sources give you the raw, direct data and methods straight from the team that did the actual study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why should a nurse manager figure out the exact type of conflict happening?

options.A: To decide which nurse should be fired
options.B: To punish the staff members involved
options.C: To pinpoint the true source of friction
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital paperwork

explanation: Spotting the right category helps leaders fix the actual root cause instead of just treating surface drama. Spot on! [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which item is essential to include in a basic home emergency supply kit?

options.A: Decorative scented candles
options.B: Large collection of reading books
options.C: Extra television remote controls
options.D: Flashlight and clean drinking water

explanation: During power outages or natural disasters, safe drinking water and light sources are vital for basic survival and safety. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h8)

question: Why do patients with newly discovered vulval cysts often feel very anxious?

options.A: Doctors usually misdiagnose it as a severe systemic infection
options.B: It automatically causes total infertility in young women
options.C: They frequently mistake the lump for a cancerous growth
options.D: The condition always requires immediate emergency surgery

explanation: Finding any unexplained lump can be scary! Patients often worry about cancer right away until a nurse or doctor calmly explains that it is benign. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h1)

question: What is the big advantage of giving tumor chemotherapy through an artery instead of a vein?

options.A: It completely eliminates all side effects throughout the entire body
options.B: It delivers a higher concentration of the drug directly to the tumor site
options.C: It prevents the drug from ever entering the systemic circulation
options.D: It allows the patient to take the chemotherapy medication at home

explanation: Think of it like dropping the medicine right on the doorstep of the problem! It gives the tumor a concentrated dose before the blood carries it away. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T13#GNS125_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of assertive communication?

options.A: Placing patient needs above all laws
options.B: Winning every professional argument
options.C: Expressing needs while respecting others
options.D: Avoiding all forms of workplace conflict

explanation: Assertiveness balances your own rights and needs with respect for the rights and needs of the people around you. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h1)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to create a private, gentle setting during a perineal check?

options.A: Bright lighting interferes with visualizing superficial blood vessels
options.B: Perineal tissue is too fragile to touch without numbing agents
options.C: Patients frequently feel embarrassed about intimate examinations
options.D: Hospital policy strictly forbids family members from staying

explanation: Checking someone's private areas can feel very vulnerable. As a caring nurse, building trust and keeping things private helps your patient feel safe and respected. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h4)

question: How are typical primary sensory neurons classified based on their structure?

options.A: Multipolar
options.B: Unipolar
options.C: Bipolar
options.D: Anaxonic

explanation: Correct! Most sensory neurons are unipolar, meaning they have a single main branch that splits into two directions—one toward the body and one toward the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h2)

question: A male patient has enlarged breast tissue during a routine check. Which body system is likely involved?

options.A: The musculoskeletal system
options.B: The urinary system
options.C: The endocrine system
options.D: The integumentary system

explanation: You nailed it! Gynecomastia (enlarged male breast tissue) is usually driven by hormone imbalances, which fall under the endocrine system. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why do nurse researchers test ideas carefully before changing how care is given on the ward?

options.A: To guarantee that all patients recover within twenty-four hours
options.B: To ensure new patient care practices are genuinely effective
options.C: To make sure that paperwork takes longer than direct patient care
options.D: To prevent any nurse from ever questioning hospital management

explanation: Spot on! We want to make sure a new care method truly works and helps our patients before we roll it out across the hospital. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T15#GNS217_U4_T15_h1)

question: During a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis, what mainly causes the airway to block?

options.A: Collapse of a main artery in the chest
options.B: Swelling in the throat and tight airways in the lungs
options.C: Paralysis of the diaphragm from fever
options.D: A buildup of thick yellow mucus in the stomach

explanation: The throat swells up and the small breathing tubes in the lungs squeeze shut, making it hard to breathe air in. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is a major environmental sign of high health risk in a community?

options.A: Having a high level of formal education
options.B: Living in a modern, well-ventilated apartment block
options.C: Lack of clean drinking water and poor sanitation
options.D: Regular attendance at routine antenatal clinics

explanation: Unsafe surroundings like bad drainage, dirty water, and poor waste disposal put everyone at risk of waterborne diseases. Spotting these early is a key part of community health! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h2)

question: Which phase of the disaster management cycle focuses right away on saving lives?

options.A: Mitigation
options.B: Preparedness
options.C: Recovery
options.D: Response

explanation: The response phase happens during or immediately after the emergency, focusing on urgent rescues and keeping people safe. You've got this! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h1)

question: What does the abbreviation HAI stand for in nursing practice?

options.A: High acuity illness
options.B: Hygiene assessment indicator
options.C: Healthcare-associated infection
options.D: Hospital antiseptic index

explanation: HAIs are infections patients acquire while receiving medical treatment in a hospital or clinic facility. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h8)

question: What is the best way for a community nurse to stop the spread of diarrhoea in a village?

options.A: Providing mosquito nets for sleeping areas at night
options.B: Teaching proper handwashing with soap and safe water storage
options.C: Inspecting local houses for structural roof damage
options.D: Distributing high-dose antibiotic capsules to all households

explanation: Diarrhoea germs usually spread through the faecal-oral route via dirty hands and water. Simple hygiene education and clean water storage save lives! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h7)

question: Which of these is a calcium channel blocker commonly prescribed for high blood pressure?

options.A: Propranolol
options.B: Verapamil
options.C: Amlodipine
options.D: Diltiazem

explanation: That's right! Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that relaxes blood vessels so blood flows more easily. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T2#GNS223_U1_T2_h5)

question: How are parents viewed within the framework of family-centered home care?

options.A: As passive observers during medical treatments
options.B: As temporary assistants to the visiting nurse
options.C: As essential frontline providers of daily care
options.D: As secondary sources of medical information

explanation: Exactly! Parents are the ones handling daily care between nurse visits, making them absolute VIPs on the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h2)

question: A nurse manager wants to reduce medication handover delays. What is the best action during the Plan phase?

options.A: Decide on a specific new handover format and plan who will test it on the morning shift
options.B: Wait for a major audit to tell the ward whether their handovers are too slow
options.C: Fire the nurses who take too long during their shift change reports
options.D: Immediately order all nurses to stop talking during handovers starting today

explanation: Spot on! Good planning means picking a specific idea and testing it on a single shift before making big changes. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why do joint contractures happen in patients with severe paralysis?

options.A: Nerves regenerate too quickly and pull the joints out of place
options.B: Joint cartilage dissolves from lack of blood circulation
options.C: Bones grow too fast because they do not bear any body weight
options.D: Muscles and tendons shorten due to a lack of movement and stretching

explanation: If a joint isn't moved through its range of motion, the soft tissues adapt by shrinking up, freezing the joint in one position. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h6)

question: What does it mean when a medication and a diluent are incompatible and form a precipitate?

options.A: Solid particles form and turn the mixture cloudy
options.B: The temperature of the syringe drops drastically
options.C: The mixture changes into a harmless gas bubbles
options.D: The volume of the liquid increases on its own

explanation: Precipitation creates solid particles or crystals in the fluid, which can cause dangerous blockages if injected into the body. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h2)

question: Which of the following is part of routine safety monitoring for someone on long-term ARVs?

options.A: Performing a daily chest X-ray to look for bone fractures
options.B: Repeating HIV testing every single week to see if the virus is gone
options.C: Checking kidney and liver function tests regularly alongside clinical screenings
options.D: Checking the patient's blood pressure only when they report chest pain

explanation: Well done! Since ARVs are processed by the body over years, we run periodic liver and kidney lab tests to catch any organ strain early. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h6)

question: What is a major reason for giving a neuromuscular blocker during emergency intubation?

options.A: To relax vocal cords and jaw muscles for safe tube placement
options.B: To help the patient clear thick mucus secretions from the lungs
options.C: To stimulate the patient to breathe deeply on their own without help
options.D: To instantly reverse dangerous drops in systemic blood pressure

explanation: Relaxing the jaw and vocal cords makes sliding the breathing tube in much smoother, protecting the patient's airway and throat from trauma. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which simple tool does a community health nurse use to listen to the baby's heartbeat during a home visit?

options.A: A sphygmomanometer
options.B: An ophthalmoscope
options.C: A percussion hammer
options.D: A Pinard stethoscope

explanation: A Pinard stethoscope (or portable Doppler) is your trusty companion in the field for checking fetal heart tones! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T4#GNS225_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do PHC workers in rural areas often rely on basic tools and good clinical judgment?

options.A: Advanced medical equipment is rarely available at the grassroots level
options.B: Guidelines forbid primary workers from using modern technology
options.C: Basic tools are proven to be more accurate than machines
options.D: Rural patients refuse to let doctors use machines

explanation: Spot on! Because primary health clinics often operate with limited resources, nurses and health workers learn to use their core clinical skills to help patients brilliantly. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is a great example of modern digital tech used in nursing education today?

options.A: Virtual reality software for viewing detailed human anatomy
options.B: Passing paper textbook chapters around a crowded classroom
options.C: Using a chalkboard to draw basic diagrams of bone fractures
options.D: Writing physical notes with ink on animal skin parchment

explanation: VR and digital apps take learning to a whole new level by bringing 3D depth to complex topics like human anatomy. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h5)

question: How do educators officially define true "learning"?

options.A: A permanent change in behavior or knowledge from experience
options.B: Attending all scheduled classroom lectures and clinicals
options.C: Memorizing facts for a nursing board examination
options.D: The physical growth of the brain during young adulthood

explanation: Learning isn't just about growing older or cramming for a test—it's when your actual knowledge or actions shift because of real experiences. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h1)

question: How does Crohn's disease affect the bowel wall differently from Ulcerative Colitis?

options.A: Crohn's affects the full thickness of the wall, while colitis affects only the mucosa
options.B: Crohn's causes smooth continuous inflammation, while colitis causes patchy skip lesions
options.C: Crohn's affects only the rectum, while colitis affects the small intestine
options.D: Crohn's only causes mild irritation, while colitis always causes complete perforation

explanation: Great job! Crohn's disease goes deep, affecting all layers of the bowel wall (transmural), whereas Ulcerative Colitis stays on the inner lining surface. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h3)

question: What do indirect health care costs mainly refer to?

options.A: Lost economic productivity and wages due to illness
options.B: The cost of ambulance fuel during emergency transport
options.C: Utility bills and building maintenance for the clinic
options.D: The price of surgical equipment bought by the facility

explanation: Indirect costs are about the money and work time lost when sickness keeps someone away from their job. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h3)

question: What do we call the amino acids that our bodies cannot make and must get from food?

options.A: Complete amino acids
options.B: Endogenous amino acids
options.C: Essential amino acids
options.D: Primary amino acids

explanation: Because our bodies can't manufacture essential amino acids on their own, it is 'essential' that we eat them in our daily diet! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h3)

question: Why might private clinics push for more injections in a fee-for-service system?

options.A: Government subsidies pay hospitals more for oral pills.
options.B: Insurance companies strictly forbid giving prescriptions for tablets.
options.C: Injections and related supplies allow them to charge higher fees.
options.D: Needles and syringes are completely free for medical facilities.

explanation: Financial gain drives unnecessary injections when clinics profit from charging extra for procedural administration and supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why do low-income communities often experience higher rates of endemic waterborne diseases?

options.A: Overcrowded schools running multiple shifts daily
options.B: Lack of proper sanitation infrastructure and safe drinking water
options.C: Higher consumption of locally brewed herbal beverages
options.D: Greater resistance of local bacteria to standard antibiotics

explanation: Without clean water systems and proper sewage disposal, water sources easily become contaminated with disease-causing microorganisms. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h4)

question: Which brain chemical is the main driver behind the 'reward loop' when we use gadgets?

options.A: Serotonin
options.B: Melatonin
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Acetylcholine

explanation: Dopamine is our feel-good chemical! Every time a notification pops up or we get a like, dopamine rewards our brain, making us want to check our phones again and again. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h3)

question: Which hormones keep milk production on hold during pregnancy?

options.A: Thyroxine and adrenaline
options.B: Prolactin and oxytocin
options.C: Estrogen and progesterone
options.D: Insulin and cortisol

explanation: Well done! High levels of these pregnancy hormones help the breasts grow, but they block actual milk flow until the baby is born. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T18#GNS121_U5_T18_h2)

question: What effect does staying in school usually have on a young girl's future marriage and childbirth?

options.A: It has no measurable impact on family planning or marriage timelines
options.B: It delays the age of marriage and first childbirth
options.C: It causes both marriage and childbirth to happen at a much earlier age
options.D: It forces young girls to completely abandon the idea of marriage

explanation: Spot on! Staying in school empowers girls and naturally encourages them to wait until a safer, more mature age before starting a family. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T47#GNS214_U1_T47_h2)

question: What does PMTCT stand for in maternal and child health nursing?

options.A: Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission
options.B: Primary Medical Treatment and Care Techniques
options.C: Pediatric Medication Testing and Clinical Trials
options.D: Post-Natal Maternal Complication Treatment

explanation: PMTCT stands for Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission, which encompasses strategies to stop vertical HIV spread during pregnancy, birth, and breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h7)

question: How does poor hospital infrastructure affect a nurse's daily shift?

options.A: It forces nurses to spend more time improvising care due to missing tools
options.B: It guarantees that nurses will receive higher hazard allowances
options.C: It reduces the total number of patients seeking medical attention
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for patient documentation

explanation: Nigerian nurses are masters of improvisation! When basic equipment is missing, you have to think on your feet to keep patients safe. That takes true skill. [learn more](GST322_U3_T6#GST322_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which gland pumps adrenaline (epinephrine) straight into the blood during a scare?

options.A: Thyroid gland
options.B: Pancreas
options.C: Adrenal medulla
options.D: Pituitary gland

explanation: The inner part of your adrenal gland (the medulla) acts fast, releasing epinephrine into the bloodstream to back up your nervous system during a rush. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T30#GNS211_U3_T30_h4)

question: In public health, what does disease 'eradication' mean?

options.A: Replacing all synthetic drugs with natural remedies
options.B: Treating all infected patients with herbal medicines
options.C: Worldwide reduction of the infection incidence to zero
options.D: Reduction of cases to zero in a single country only

explanation: Eradication means completely and permanently wiping out the germ and its reservoir everywhere on planet Earth. Gone for good! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is improvisation a valuable skill for a nursing educator working in a resource-limited setting?

options.A: It guarantees that students will pass board exams on the first try
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical hospital postings
options.C: It is always superior to factory-made medical equipment
options.D: It overcomes financial shortages without sacrificing student learning

explanation: Improvisation allows educators to deliver practical, high-quality lessons even when funds for buying commercial teaching aids are limited. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h6)

question: Why is the IASC framework designed as a pyramid rather than a square?

options.A: To illustrate that basic community needs affect a larger population than specialized care
options.B: To prove that physical safety is less important than psychiatric medications
options.C: To show that specialized services are needed by the majority of the population
options.D: To demonstrate that doctors must handle every level of community distress

explanation: Think of it like a crowd: the wide base at the bottom represents everyday survival needs that affect almost everyone, while the narrow top shows specialized care needed by fewer people. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why does a Root Cause Analysis look beyond individual staff error?

options.A: Because government laws forbid blaming nurses for bad patient outcomes
options.B: Because hospital managers want to protect nurses from losing their licenses
options.C: Because most errors are caused by weak systems, equipment flaws, or poor processes
options.D: Because individual mistakes are impossible to prove in a court of law

explanation: RCA looks at the big picture because fixing a broken system prevents future errors much better than simply blaming a worker. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h5)

question: What happens when homeostatic failure is left untreated for too long?

options.A: Vital organs begin to shut down and shock can occur
options.B: The patient enters a state of deep relaxation
options.C: The body automatically fixes itself without any help
options.D: Blood pressure rises to a very safe level

explanation: Spot on. If the body's regulatory systems stay broken down, tissues are starved of oxygen, which can quickly lead to organ failure and shock. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h7)

question: A student nurse visiting an elderly client notices a slippery bathtub with no support rails. What is the best immediate safety action?

options.A: Recommend installing grab bars and using a non-slip bath mat
options.B: Advise the client to stop bathing completely during the week
options.C: Tell the family to remodel the entire house immediately
options.D: Suggest moving the client to a hospital right away

explanation: Great choice! Adding simple items like grab bars and non-slip mats fixes the danger right away without needing drastic changes like moving out. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h3)

question: Between which two vertebrae is a lumbar puncture usually performed in adults?

options.A: S1-S2 or S2-S3
options.B: L3-L4 or L4-L5
options.C: C1-C2 or C2-C3
options.D: T11-T12 or T12-L1

explanation: Correct! These lower spaces are chosen because the main spinal cord has already ended there, making the needle stick much safer. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h2)

question: How would you simply define a 'nursing theory'?

options.A: A strict set of disciplinary rules for student nurses
options.B: A proven drug recipe used in emergency rooms
options.C: An organized set of concepts explaining a phenomenon
options.D: A list of hospital equipment costs for the year

explanation: Correct! A theory gives us a helpful framework to explain why things happen and guides our nursing actions. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T1#GNS217_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main job of micronutrients in the human body?

options.A: Providing the primary source of daily calories
options.B: Building large muscle mass quickly
options.C: Storing excess body fat for warmth
options.D: Regulating chemical reactions and body processes

explanation: Even though we only need them in tiny amounts, vitamins and minerals (micronutrients) act like spark plugs to keep our body processes running smoothly. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h3)

question: What should you do if the chosen injection site has an open sore or infection?

options.A: Warm the skin with a hot pack to improve blood flow
options.B: Choose a different healthy site for the injection
options.C: Use a longer needle to bypass the damaged area
options.D: Clean the sore with extra antiseptic before piercing

explanation: Always protect broken skin! Finding a healthy site prevents spreading infection and helps the medication absorb properly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T3#GNS122_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do public health nurses look at mental health through a collective lens rather than just an individual one?

options.A: A person's state of mind is deeply connected to their environment and living conditions
options.B: Individual therapy sessions are too expensive for community clinics to fund
options.C: Group counseling is the only proven method to treat depression
options.D: Government policies require nurses to ignore personal medical histories

explanation: Because people are influenced by their surroundings, housing, and social networks, community nurses must evaluate the broader environment to understand mental well-being. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h1)

question: When studying how patients cope with long-term illness, why are interviews often better than rigid surveys?

options.A: Interviews allow participants to explain things in their own words
options.B: Surveys are too expensive to print out in hospital wards
options.C: Interviews do not require any ethical review board approval
options.D: Surveys only work when patients are unconscious

explanation: Spot on! People aren't checkboxes. Letting patients talk freely gives you rich insights that a standard survey would completely miss. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h1)

question: What does the term 'aging in place' mean for elderly patients?

options.A: Traveling across the country without any medical help
options.B: Staying in the emergency room for extended observation
options.C: Living safely in one's own home rather than a facility
options.D: Moving into a large hospital permanently

explanation: Aging in place refers to older adults remaining in their private residences while receiving needed support services. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h4)

question: How does the principle of harmony of objectives help a hospital ward?

options.A: It removes the need for performance appraisals entirely
options.B: It forces every nurse to work identical shift schedules
options.C: It ensures all nurses sing together during morning handover
options.D: It helps staff achieve personal goals while meeting hospital aims

explanation: When personal aspirations align with institutional goals, staff are happier and work harder for patient outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h2)

question: A patient suffers a severe spinal cord injury at the level of C2. What major complication do you anticipate?

options.A: Paralysis of the lower legs while retaining full upper body movement
options.B: Inability to move the facial muscles while breathing remains normal
options.C: Loss of sensation only in the hands and lower arms
options.D: Inability to breathe independently due to loss of phrenic nerve function

explanation: Since the phrenic nerve depends on C3 to C5 to function, an injury higher up at C2 cuts off the brain's breathing signals to the diaphragm. Patient safety first! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h4)

question: Which of these is a great example of the 'Right Assessment' in action?

options.A: Checking blood pressure before giving an antihypertensive drug
options.B: Asking the patient what their favorite food is for breakfast
options.C: Cleaning the bedside table before placing a water cup
options.D: Reading the hospital policy manual on intravenous access

explanation: Right assessment means checking vital signs or lab results first to make sure the drug is actually safe to give right now. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of breaking any link in the chain of infection?

options.A: To make the patient immune to all known viruses
options.B: To completely sterilize the human skin permanently
options.C: To cure a chronic illness without using antibiotics
options.D: To stop the transmission of infectious diseases

explanation: Interrupting even one link in the chain stops the microbe from reaching a new host and spreading disease. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h1)

question: Why is it important for nurses to use standard nutritional terms?

options.A: It allows nurses to cook meals for patients.
options.B: It prevents dangerous misunderstandings among the healthcare team.
options.C: It completely replaces the need for blood tests.
options.D: It speeds up the hospital discharge process.

explanation: Great job! Using clear, standard words means doctors, nurses, and dietitians are all on the same page, keeping your patients safe. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h1)

question: A farmer arrives at the clinic drooling, tearing up, peeing frequently, and having muscle twitches after spraying the farm. What is this?

options.A: Sedative overdose from sleeping pills
options.B: Cholinergic poisoning from organophosphates
options.C: Caustic poisoning from swallowed acid
options.D: Opioid poisoning from strong painkillers

explanation: Correct! Remember the DUMBELS sign (drooling, urination, muscle twitching, etc.)—it points straight to organophosphate poisoning. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h4)

question: What is the heart of equity in healthcare financing?

options.A: Private hospitals should receive more government subsidies than public clinics
options.B: Access to care should be based on health needs rather than the ability to pay
options.C: Every citizen must pay an identical flat fee for hospital registration
options.D: Urban residents must have priority access to surgical specialists

explanation: Equity is about fairness. Your wallet shouldn't decide whether you live or die. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to start talking with a patient who has just suffered a heavy loss?

options.A: Provide a printed checklist of grief stages for the patient to fill out
options.B: Wait in silence until the patient explicitly asks for medical advice
options.C: Tell the patient about your own personal losses to build quick rapport
options.D: Ask open-ended questions and listen actively to the patient's story

explanation: You got it! Open-ended questions open the door for patients to share their unique story without feeling pressured or rushed. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h5)

question: What does 'accessibility' mean when we talk about community health services?

options.A: Services are restricted to wealthy individuals who can pay cash
options.B: Care reaches marginalized and remote populations without discrimination
options.C: Clinics remain closed on weekends to protect staff schedules
options.D: Patients must travel long distances to reach urban tertiary centers

explanation: Well done! Accessibility means making sure that healthcare breaks down barriers—whether financial or geographical—so that everyone who needs care can actually get it. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h2)

question: What is considered the gold standard proof that your autoclave actually killed all microbial spores?

options.A: Visual inspection of clean instruments for water spots
options.B: Digital gauge printouts showing chamber temperature and pressure
options.C: Chemical indicator tape placed on the outside of peel packs
options.D: Biological indicators containing resistant bacterial spores

explanation: Nothing beats testing with actual heat-resistant spores! If the autoclave can kill these test spores, we know it's doing its job properly. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why must nurses stress to parents the importance of finishing a child's entire course of antibiotics?

options.A: To prevent the child from developing a skin rash
options.B: To permanently boost the child's daily appetite
options.C: To completely wipe out the bacteria and prevent relapse
options.D: To ensure the child gains healthy weight rapidly

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early just because the child 'looks better' can let hidden bacteria bounce back and cause more kidney damage. Patient education at its finest! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h9)

question: Which systemic autoimmune condition is a common underlying cause of chronic glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Systemic lupus erythematosus
options.B: Chronic asthma
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis only

explanation: Lupus (SLE) is a well-known condition where the body's immune system attacks its own tissues, very frequently targeting the delicate filters in the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T5#GNS213_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is a major challenge that family caregivers often face when looking after a sick relative at home?

options.A: Burnout and physical exhaustion
options.B: Over-staffing by professional nurses
options.C: Excessive financial compensation
options.D: Too much free time and boredom

explanation: Exactly right. Caregiver fatigue is real! Looking after a loved one without a break can easily lead to physical and emotional burnout. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h6)

question: What severe complication happens when an intestinal ulcer eats all the way through the bowel wall?

options.A: Intestinal perforation
options.B: Chronic kidney failure
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Hepatic encephalopathy

explanation: You nailed it! A break through the entire bowel wall is called a perforation—definitely a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h6)

question: Which principle of intersectoral collaboration focuses on putting the most vulnerable people first?

options.A: Specialization
options.B: Privatization
options.C: Equity
options.D: Centralization

explanation: You've got it! Equity means fairness—making sure resources and care reach the people who need them the most, rather than just splitting everything equally. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h2)

question: Which food group is most helpful to prevent constipation in older adults who aren't very active?

options.A: Simple sugars
options.B: Animal proteins
options.C: Dietary fiber
options.D: Saturated fats

explanation: Great thinking! Fiber adds bulk to stool and keeps things moving smoothly, helping make up for slower digestion in older age. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T4#GNS321_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which test is mostly used to confirm if a patient has fluid or consolidation in their lungs?

options.A: Chest X-ray
options.B: Abdominal ultrasound
options.C: Electrocardiogram
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging

explanation: A simple chest X-ray is fast, easy, and gives a clear picture of cloudy areas or fluid buildup in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h5)

question: A patient keeps coming back to the hospital, and you notice relatives arguing loudly at the bedside. How would Family Systems Theory explain this?

options.A: The family tension at home is slowing down the patient's recovery
options.B: The patient is ignoring medication just to annoy people
options.C: The doctors failed to find the main physical illness
options.D: The hospital building is the only reason they are arguing

explanation: Stress at home gets under a patient's skin! Unresolved arguments and family tension can genuinely hold back physical healing. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why are gravies and sauces often added to meats on a soft diet?

options.A: To hide the taste of spoiled ingredients in the kitchen
options.B: To add moisture and prevent the meat from feeling dry during chewing
options.C: To change the color of the food to stimulate appetite
options.D: To dramatically increase the sodium content for hydration

explanation: Soft meats can easily become dry and difficult to swallow; gravies provide necessary lubrication. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h4)

question: What is septicemia?

options.A: Presence of multiplying bacteria in the bloodstream
options.B: Inflammation limited to the outer layer of skin
options.C: A localized collection of pus in a single muscle
options.D: Sudden paralysis caused by a damaged nerve

explanation: Septicemia happens when bacteria get past local defenses and start multiplying in the general blood circulation, making the patient very ill all over. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which organization sets the foundational legal and professional practice boundaries for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: National Union of Local Government Employees
options.B: West African Health Education Board
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
options.D: Nigerian Medical Association Financial Committee

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should do right away for a patient with sudden chest pain?

options.A: Administering supplemental oxygen
options.B: Having the patient rest immediately
options.C: Encouraging heavy physical exercise
options.D: Checking vital signs and an ECG

explanation: You got it! Exercise makes the heart work harder and crave more oxygen, which is the last thing an ischemic heart needs. Rest is always first! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h6)

question: Why do we use injectable (parenteral) artesunate for severe, complicated malaria instead of oral drugs?

options.A: It achieves rapid systemic drug levels when the child cannot safely swallow
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for nursing monitoring
options.C: It has zero side effects compared to oral tablets
options.D: It cures the infection permanently in a single minute

explanation: When a child is vomiting or too weak to swallow, injections get the life-saving medicine directly into the bloodstream fast. Excellent nursing judgment! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h4)

question: What is the main building role of lipids in our bodies?

options.A: Building the outer layer of every cell
options.B: Acting as enzymes to speed up reactions
options.C: Providing quick energy for the brain
options.D: Carrying water-soluble vitamins in the blood

explanation: You've got this! Phospholipids and cholesterol act like tiny bricks that form the protective wall (membrane) around all our cells. Great job! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T011#GNS227_U4_T011_h1)

question: What is the official color of the standard ADR reporting form used by NAFDAC?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: White
options.C: Green
options.D: Blue

explanation: You'll see this often in practice! The NAFDAC Yellow Form is the standard, easily recognizable document used across Nigeria for reporting bad drug reactions. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why is staff health considered a key component of the School Health Programme?

options.A: Staff members consume the majority of school meals
options.B: Adults are more prone to infections than young children
options.C: Teachers are legally required to work twenty-four hours daily
options.D: Healthy staff serve as role models and maintain productivity

explanation: Staff well-being directly impacts the quality of teaching and ensures that adults model healthy behaviors for students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why are peer champions so valuable for sustaining long-term changes in a nursing unit?

options.A: They write all the hospital policies and clinical guidelines.
options.B: They handle the payroll and administrative duties for the ward.
options.C: They model the new behaviors and encourage their colleagues.
options.D: They are responsible for punishing staff who refuse to comply.

explanation: Peer champions lead by example on the floor, making it much easier for other nurses to adopt new ways with confidence. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h7)

question: How would you best describe peristalsis?

options.A: Wave-like muscle contractions that push food forward
options.B: Localized churning that mixes food in the small intestine
options.C: The absorption of water through the large bowel wall
options.D: The secretion of digestive enzymes by the pancreas

explanation: Spot on! Think of peristalsis like a wave of muscle squeezes moving food steadily along down the digestive tube. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which lobe of the brain is responsible for processing final visual images?

options.A: Temporal lobe
options.B: Occipital lobe
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Parietal lobe

explanation: The visual cortex, which interprets incoming signals as sight, is located in the occipital lobe at the back of the head. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do you need your nursing clinical judgment when reading a scatter diagram?

options.A: To calculate the exact square root of every data point
options.B: To draw the axes without using a ruler or computer
options.C: To eliminate the need for any further statistical tests
options.D: To decide if the visual relationship makes biological sense

explanation: Always ask yourself: does this relationship actually make sense in real healthcare practice, or is it just a random coincidence? [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving emergency contraception to a survivor of sexual assault?

options.A: To lower the patient's blood pressure during panic attacks
options.B: To prevent an unwanted pregnancy resulting from the assault
options.C: To instantly stop acute physical bleeding from internal wounds
options.D: To cure existing sexually transmitted bacterial infections

explanation: Emergency contraception is time-sensitive and given within a 120-hour window specifically to stop pregnancy from happening after an assault. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T11#GNS312_U4_T11_h6)

question: A nurse wants to lower catheter-related infections in the surgical ward. Following research principles, what should be done first?

options.A: Stop using catheters entirely for every single surgical patient
options.B: Review current research for evidence-based catheter care guidelines
options.C: Wait for patient complaints before changing the cleaning routine
options.D: Punish staff members who report high infection numbers

explanation: Spot on! Whenever we want to solve a clinical problem, checking current research helps us find safe, proven protocols that actually work. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is a major negative effect of HIV-related stigma in our communities?

options.A: It eliminates the need for VCT clinics.
options.B: It discourages people from getting tested or seeking treatment.
options.C: It increases the effectiveness of antiretroviral drugs.
options.D: It causes the HIV virus to mutate into a weaker strain.

explanation: Fear of being judged makes people hide their status and stay away from clinics. Compassion and education are our best tools to fight this stigma! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h9)

question: Why must a pharmacy balance full cost recovery with making drugs affordable?

options.A: To prevent private pharmacies from suing the hospital for unfair competition
options.B: To ensure the doctors receive a bonus for prescribing cheaper medications
options.C: To comply with international laws governing pharmaceutical manufacturing
options.D: To make sure vulnerable patients can still afford their essential treatments

explanation: If drug prices climb too high, everyday patients won't be able to buy them, which defeats the whole public health mission of our hospitals. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary role of autotrophic microbes in natural water bodies?

options.A: Increasing water turbidity and cloudiness
options.B: Causing severe water-borne infections
options.C: Performing photosynthesis to produce oxygen
options.D: Dissolving heavy metals in the sediment

explanation: Autotrophic microbes contain chlorophyll and produce oxygen just like land plants, supporting aquatic life. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h2)

question: When we talk about 'psychosocial' care in mental health nursing, what two main things are we bringing together?

options.A: Laboratory values and physical symptoms
options.B: Emotional experiences and environmental conditions
options.C: Surgical history and genetic mutations
options.D: Medication side effects and dietary habits

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial care looks at both sides of the coin: what is happening inside a person's mind (psychological) and what is happening in their world outside (social). [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h1)

question: What is the main goal of Youth Friendly Services (YFS)?

options.A: To provide free medical treatment only for children
options.B: To attract and address the health needs of adolescents
options.C: To make hospitals run faster and more efficiently
options.D: To replace adult medical care entirely

explanation: You got it! YFS is all about creating a safe space tailored to the unique physical and emotional needs of young people. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h1)

question: How does stomach pain from a gastric ulcer usually behave compared to a duodenal ulcer?

options.A: Gastric ulcer pain often worsens soon after eating food.
options.B: Gastric ulcer pain is relieved by eating meals.
options.C: Duodenal ulcer pain gets worse immediately during a meal.
options.D: Duodenal ulcer pain never occurs at night.

explanation: Correct! Food triggers acid release, which immediately irritates a gastric ulcer. Duodenal ulcers, on the other hand, often feel better temporarily when food is in the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why should nurses advise patients to stay off their phones or TVs right before trying to sleep?

options.A: Watching shows late at night leads to weight gain
options.B: Screen use causes severe dehydration in the eyes
options.C: Electronic devices consume too much electricity in the bedroom
options.D: The bright light from screens tricks the brain into staying awake

explanation: The blue light from phone and TV screens blocks melatonin, the natural hormone that tells our brain it's time to sleep. Put the phone away for a better night's rest! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h7)

question: A study compares lung cancer patients with healthy people, looking backward at their past smoking habits. What kind of study is this?

options.A: Prospective cohort study
options.B: Qualitative ethnography
options.C: Case-control study
options.D: Randomized controlled trial

explanation: Think of a case-control study as looking in the rearview mirror. You start with the 'cases' (people who have the condition) and look backward at their past exposures compared to healthy controls. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h5)

question: What action should a nurse take when a sharps container reaches its designated fill line?

options.A: Leave it open on the counter until the end of the working week
options.B: Seal and close the container securely for safe disposal
options.C: Push the needles down firmly with a gloved hand to create more space
options.D: Transfer some of the used needles into a regular plastic trash bag

explanation: Containers must be closed and replaced once they reach the fill line to prevent accidental overflows and needle injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the major danger of failing to treat puerperal sepsis promptly?

options.A: Immediate closure of the fallopian tubes
options.B: Development of chronic gestational diabetes
options.C: Permanent discoloration of the skin and hair
options.D: Progression to septic shock and multi-organ failure

explanation: An infection left unchecked in the uterus won't just stay there—it can spread through the whole body, causing a dangerous drop in blood pressure and organ failure. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h8)

question: Why do many psychiatric patients try alternative healing methods?

options.A: To reduce medication side effects and gain personal control
options.B: To avoid speaking with healthcare providers entirely
options.C: To increase the cost of their psychiatric treatment
options.D: To completely replace all forms of medical documentation

explanation: Patients often explore natural or alternative therapies to feel better while avoiding harsh drug side effects, and it helps them feel more involved in their own recovery! [learn more](GNS314_U4_T3#GNS314_U4_T3_h1)
